questions.text: Which items are part of LLM scale?
options: Parameters, data, and compute
Generality, Context, and Compute
IE, IR, and RAG
Vocabulary size, Tokens, and Training Corpora
questions.feedback: Scale includes model parameters, training data, and computational resources.

questions.text: What does nuanced instruction following mean?
options: Responding to detailed user directions with appropriate behavior
Out of context response generation
use appropriate model to understand the user prompt
Ignoring the prompt and returning appropriate behavior
questions.answer: Responding to detailed user directions with appropriate behavior
questions.feedback: Nuanced instruction following means using the prompt details to guide the response.

questions.text: Match each limitation with its meaning.

pairs.definition: Plausible but factually wrong output
Static training data without real-time awareness
Failure on unfamiliar logical patterns
Reflection or amplification of problematic training patterns

questions.text: Match each Transformer component with its role.

pairs.definition: Refines each token representation
Adds order information
Relates tokens inside the same sequence
Converts a token into a vector

questions.text: Why are very large parameter counts important for LLMs?
options: They make the model ignore language patterns
They force the model to use only symbolic rules
They remove the need for training data
Some capabilities appear only after critical scale thresholds
questions.answer: Some capabilities appear only after critical scale thresholds
questions.feedback: Beyond certain scales, models may show new capabilities such as reasoning or instruction following.

questions.text: What is a benefit of more parameters in an LLM?
options: They force the positional information of tokens to be considered
They remove the need for tokens inside the model
They allow storage of more nuanced patterns and knowledge
They make the model Huge and accept multi-modality
questions.answer: They allow storage of more nuanced patterns and knowledge
questions.feedback: More parameters increase capacity for nuanced patterns and knowledge.

questions.text: Match each property with the correct description.

pairs.definition: One pre-trained model adapts to many tasks
Predictable improvement when scale factors increase together
Learning from prompt examples without weight updates
Parameters, data, and compute

questions.text: Which set lists the three defining properties of modern LLMs?
options: Bias Toxicity, and Compute Cost
Hallucination, Knowledge Cut-off, and Context Limits
Scale, generality, and in-context learning
Encoder, Decoder, and Embedding
questions.feedback: The three properties are scale, generality, and in-context learning.

questions.text: In-context learning requires gradient updates to the model weights during the prompt.
questions.feedback: In-context learning uses examples in the prompt without changing weights.

questions.text: What does cross-lingual transfer help a model do?
options: Use multiple tokens for each word in training
Convert every word into the multiple tokens
Apply learned language patterns across different languages
Train the model on multiple language
questions.answer: Apply learned language patterns across different languages
questions.feedback: Cross-lingual transfer supports performance across languages.

questions.text: Self-attention helps a model relate words to other words in the same sequence.
What does generality mean for a pre-trained LLM?
options: The model trained on general data and knowledge
The model works generally without user interaction
A model can answer a general response to the prompt
One model can adapt to thousands of tasks
questions.answer: One model can adapt to thousands of tasks
questions.feedback: Generality means a single pre-trained model can support many tasks.

questions.text: Match each core LLM term with its meaning.

pairs.definition: Capability that appears beyond a scale threshold
Training objective that predicts the following token
Word or subword unit processed by the model
Deep neural network trained on massive text corpora

questions.text: Why are dimensions such as 512, 768, 1024, or 4096 used?
options: They remove the need for vocabulary
They force every word to mean the same thing
They replace training data entirely
They provide capacity to capture subtle distinctions
questions.answer: They provide capacity to capture subtle distinctions
questions.feedback: More dimensions give capacity to represent fine-grained distinctions.

questions.text: What does greater compute enable during LLM training?
options: Processing larger models on more data
Limiting the model to few tokens and context
Avoiding all matrix multiplications
Replacing training with manual rules
questions.answer: Processing larger models on more data
questions.feedback: Greater compute enables bigger training runs over more data.

questions.text: The decoder can generate output one token at a time using previous tokens and encoder information.
questions.feedback: Decoder generation is autoregressive and can use cross-attention to the encoder.

questions.text: Which statement best describes a Large Language Model?
options: A deep neural network trained on massive text corpora to model token sequences
A hardware device designed for speech recording
A database table that stores fixed answers to every question
A rule-based grammar checker that only corrects spelling
questions.answer: A deep neural network trained on massive text corpora to model token sequences
questions.feedback: An LLM is a deep neural network trained on large text collections to model sequences of tokens.

questions.text: Multi-head attention runs several attention heads sequentially to capture different relationships.
questions.feedback: Different heads can focus on different patterns such as grammar, meaning, or position, but they run in parallel, not sequentially.

questions.text: Embedding vectors are normally obtained by looking up token IDs in a learned table.
questions.feedback: Each token ID maps to a row in the embedding table.

Reads and represents the input sequence
Prevents looking ahead during generation
Allows decoder to look at encoder outputs
